'''Yeom Han-woong''' (born 5 December 1966) is a South Korean physicist. A tenured professor at [[POSTECH]], he has led several research centers for the university and from 2013 in collaboration with the [[Institute for Basic Science]]. He is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and has served as vice chairman of the Korean government's first science and technology advisory group<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20181213132100017 |title= 염한웅 포항공대 교수 "혁신성장의 가장 큰 축은 '과학'" |last= 신 |first= 선미 |date= 12 December 2018 |website= Yonhapnews |access-date= 28 January 2019 |quote= 문재인 정부의 첫 과학기술자문회의 부의장을 맡았던 염한웅 포항공대 물리학과 교수는 13일 서울 강남구 한국과학기술회관에서 열린 '혁신성장을 위한 국가혁신체계 2019 대토론회'에서 현 정책의 문제점을 이같이 지적했다. |language= ko}}</ref> for three consecutive terms.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.news1.kr/articles/?4241695 |title= 염한웅 과기자문회의 부의장 '3연임'…"탄소중립 밑그림 그리겠다" |author= 김승준 |date= 15 March 2021 |website= News1|publisher= |access-date= 16 March 2021 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref> With more than 300 publications to his name, his research has been cited over 5,000 times giving him an [[h-index]] of 40 and [[i10-index]] of 125.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=AIl4E7IAAAAJ |title= Han Woong Yeom - Google Scholar Citations |author=<!--Not stated--> |website= [[Google Scholar]] |access-date= 28 January 2019 }}</ref>

==Career==
He was born in Seoul, and studied physics as an undergraduate at [[Seoul National University]] before going on to [[Tohoku University]] in Japan as a doctoral student. Thereafter he was a research associate at the Department of Chemistry, [[University of Tokyo]] (1996–2000). He then returned to his native South Korea, where he was an assistant/associate professor at the Department of Physics, [[Yonsei University]] (2000–2009), and then a full professor (2009–2010). During his time at Yonsei, he was part of a research team that developed a semiconductor nanometer wire with a thickness of 1 to 3 atoms.<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Choi |first1= Won Hoon |last2= Kang |first2= Pil Gyu |last3= Ryang |first3= Kyung Deuk |last4= Yeom |first4= Han Woong |title= Band-structure engineering of gold atomic wires on silicon by controlled doping |url= https://journals.aps.org/prl/pdf/10.1103/PhysRevLett.100.126801 |journal= [[Physical Review Letters]] |date= 2008 |publisher= [[American Physical Society]] |volume= 100 |issue= 12 |article-number= 126801 |doi= 10.1103/PhysRevLett.100.126801 |pmid= 18517895 |bibcode= 2008PhRvL.100l6801C |access-date= 28 January 2019|url-access= subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1= Kang |first1= Pil-Gyu |last2= Jeong |first2= Hojin |last3= Yeom |first3= Han Woong |date= 11 April 2008 |title= Hopping Domain Wall Induced by Paired Adatoms on an Atomic Wire: Si (111)−(5×2)−Au |url= https://link.aps.org/pdf/10.1103/PhysRevLett.100.146103 |journal= [[Physical Review Letters]] |publisher= [[American Physical Society]] |volume= 100 |issue= 14 |article-number= 146103 |doi= 10.1103/PhysRevLett.100.146103 |pmid= 18518054 |access-date= 28 January 2019|url-access= subscription }}</ref>

Afterwards he moved to the Department of Physics, [[POSTECH]] (2010–present), where he served as director of Center for Atomic Wires and Layers (2003–2012), director of Center for Low Dimensional Electronic Symmetries (2012–2013), and founding director of Center for Artificial Low Dimensional Electronic Systems, [[Institute for Basic Science]] (2013–present).<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.ibs.re.kr/eng/sub02_03_03.do |title= Center for Artificial Low Dimensional Electronic Systems - Physics - Research Centers |author=<!--Not stated--> |website= [[Institute for Basic Science]] |access-date= 28 January 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=herve_lemoine |url=http://www.ivc19.com/fileadmin/document/Bio/Bio_Yeom_HW.pdf |title=Prof. Han Woong Yeom |publisher=www.ivc19.com |date=1966-12-05 |access-date=2013-11-29 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160505071143/http://www.ivc19.com/fileadmin/document/Bio/Bio_Yeom_HW.pdf |archive-date=2016-05-05 }}</ref>
